items.ms: (i) B1 n = 1 gives LHS = RHS = (5 -8; 2 -3) shown explicitly, M1 multiply the assumed k-th power by the original matrix, dM1 correct un-simplified product with at least 3 correct elements, A1 reach the (k+1) form with no errors, A1 cso conclusion. (ii) B1 shows u1 = 8 and u2 = 40 from 6^n + 2^n, M1 substitute the k and k+1 forms into u(k+2) = 8u(k+1) - 12u(k), A1 express in 6^k and 2^k (36(6^k) + 4(2^k)), A1 6^(k+2) + 2^(k+2), A1 cso conclusion (true for n = k and k+1 implies k+2; true for n = 1 and 2).

items.name: Two inductions: recurrence formula and divisibility
items.how: No part ids in the input; two proofs by induction: (i) u1 = 3 and u(n+1) = 2u(n) - 2^(n+1) (printed as '2n + 1' in the extraction; reconstructed from the scheme) gives u(n) = 5 × 2^(n-1) - n × 2^n (5); (ii) f(n) = 5^(n+2) - 4n - 9 is divisible by 16 (5).
items.ms: (i) B1 n = 1 gives u1 = 3; M1 substitutes the n = k formula into the recurrence to get u(k + 1); A1 correct expanded expression 5 × 2^k - k × 2^(k+1) - 2^(k+1); A1 reaches 5 × 2^k - (k + 1)2^(k+1) with no errors; A1cso full conclusion. (ii) B1 f(1) = 112 = 16 × 7; M1 attempts f(k + 1); dM1 expresses it in terms of f(k); A1 f(k + 1) = 5f(k) + 16k + 32; A1cso full conclusion. items.name: Rational inequality with x/(2-x) and (x+3)/x
items.how: Use algebra to determine the set of values of x for which x/(2 - x) <= (x + 3)/x (form read from the scheme); solutions relying entirely on graphical methods are not acceptable.
items.ms: M1 collect to one side; M1 common denominator and A1 correct fraction (x^2 - (2 - x)(x + 3))/(x(2 - x)); B1 critical values 0 and 2; M1 solve the numerator 2x^2 + x - 6 = 0; A1 critical values 3/2 and -2; A1A1 x <= -2, 0 < x <= 3/2, x > 2 (and/or/comma between regions fine, intersection symbol not). items.name: Image of imaginary axis under Mobius map
items.how: The transformation w = ((2 + i)z + 4)/(z - i), z not equal to i, maps the imaginary axis in the z-plane onto line l in the w-plane. Determine a Cartesian equation of l in the form au + bv + c = 0 with integers a, b, c.
items.ms: M1 make z the subject and A1 z = (wi + 4)/(w - 2 - i); M1 w = u + iv and multiply by the conjugate of the denominator; dM1 set the real part to zero; A1 any correct equation; A1 3u + 2v - 8 = 0 (any integer multiple). Alternatives: z = iy and eliminate y, or map two points of the imaginary axis and find the line.

items.name: Prove reduction formula for e^x sin^n x + Evaluate e^x sin^4 x integral using reduction

items.ms: M1 apply the reduction formula once (I_4 in terms of I_2); M1 apply again and use I_0 = integral of e^x = e^x; dM1 substitute limits 0 and pi/2 and subtract; A1 (41 e^(pi/2) - 24)/85. Limits may be applied as you go (I_0 = e^(pi/2) - 1).
path: FP3.4.5 - The derivation and use of si

items.name: Eccentricity of ellipse + Foci and directrices of ellipse
items.how: Hence determine (i) the coordinates of the foci and (ii) the equations of the directrices of the ellipse.
items.ms: B1ft foci (+/- ae, 0) = (+/- sqrt5, 0) as coordinates; B1ft directrices x = +/- a/e = +/- 9/sqrt5 (equations, not just values); both follow through their e. Using a^2, b^2 consistently scores B marks as a special case.

items.name: Derivative involving arcsin 2x, then evaluate
items.how: Question text not captured in the input; from the scheme it is a differentiate-then-'hence' pair: differentiate a function whose derivative is 3 arcsin 2x + 6x/sqrt(1 - 4x^2) (product of x and arcsin 2x), then hence find the exact value of dy/dx at x = 1/4.
items.ms: M1 differentiate arcsin(kx) as 1/sqrt(1 - ...) times k and combine by the product rule; A1 correct derivative 3 arcsin 2x + 6x/sqrt(1 - 4x^2); B1 dependent on full marks in the first part: dy/dx = pi/2 + sqrt3 at x = 1/4. 'arsinh' or 'arcsinh' in place of arcsin scores M0.

items.name: Other directrix of hyperbola
items.how: Hyperbola x^2/a^2 - y^2/b^2 = 1 with one directrix given; write down an equation of the other directrix.
items.ms: B1 for the symmetric directrix x = -4/3 (the negative of the given x = 4/3), any equivalent equation.

items.name: Find a and foci of hyperbola
items.how: Determine (i) the value of a and (ii) the coordinates of each focus, given the hyperbola's equation (b^2 = 5) and a directrix x = 4/3.
items.ms: (i) M1 use a/e = 4/3 with b^2 = a^2(e^2 - 1) to form an equation in a (or e); dM1 solve the resulting 3TQ in a^2 (9a^4 - 16a^2 - 80 = 0) to a positive root; A1 a = 2 (e = 3/2) with negative rejected. (ii) M1 numerical ae (or sqrt(a^2 + b^2)); A1 foci (+/-3, 0). Part (ii) can be answered before (i).

items.name: Solve 4 tanh x minus sech x equals 1
items.how: Solve 4 tanh x - sech x = 1, giving the answer as x = ln k with k a fully simplified rational number.
items.ms: M1 replace a hyperbolic function by its exponential form (or convert to sinh and cosh); M1 A1 obtain the correct quadratic 3e^(2x) - 2e^x - 5 = 0; M1 solve for e^x (any exact form including the positive root); A1 x = ln(5/3) with no unrejected extra solutions. Squaring routes (in sinh, tanh, sech or cosh) are also credited but must reject the spurious root.
path: FP3.1.1 - Definition of the six hyperb

items.name: Integral giving arsinh then definite integral
items.how: Single question with two linked parts: (a) determine the integral of 1/sqrt(9x^2 + 16) dx; (b) hence determine the exact value of a definite integral of the same integrand (limits -2 to 2 per the scheme), in the form a ln(b + c sqrt13) with rational a, b, c.
items.ms: (a) M1 obtains p arsinh(qx) (or ln form); A1 (1/3) arsinh(3x/4) + c (arcsin or arsin is M0). (b) M1 substitute limits 2 and -2 into the antiderivative and subtract; dM1 reach a ln-form with sqrt13; A1 (2/3) ln(3/2 + sqrt13/2) or equivalent. Decimal answers are not enough.

items.name: Value of a making matrix singular
items.how: For a 3x3 matrix A containing a positive constant a, determine the exact value of a for which A is singular.
items.ms: The mark scheme in the input does not contain a matching part: its Q5 layout is (a)(i) value of a given eigenvalue 2, (a)(ii) other eigenvalues, (b) eigenvectors, (c) diagonalising P and D, so it appears to belong to the version before the question was reissued. The wording supports setting det A = 0 to get a quadratic in a and taking the positive root, but no marking points are given.

items.name: Find a and other eigenvalues
items.how: Given that 2 is an eigenvalue of A, determine (i) the value of a and (ii) the other two eigenvalues.
items.ms: (i) M1 form det(A - 2I) (or Ax = 2x); dM1 solve the quadratic a^2 + 3a - 10 = 0; A1 a = 2 (a = -5 rejected as a > 0). (ii) M1 characteristic equation with a = 2 giving a real non-zero eigenvalue; A1 eigenvalues 4 and 5 (cubic is lambda^3 - 11lambda^2 + 38lambda - 40 = 0).

items.name: Normalised eigenvectors for other eigenvalues
items.how: Given a normalised eigenvector for eigenvalue 2, determine a normalised eigenvector for each of the other two eigenvalues of A.
items.ms: M1 use Ax = lambda x with their a and a non-zero eigenvalue (not 2) to get three equations (or a cross product of two rows of A - lambda I); A1 one correct eigenvector, A1 both ((0, -1, 2) for 4 and (1, -2, 7) for 5); M1 normalise at least one; A1 both normalised: (1/sqrt5)(0, -1, 2) and (1/sqrt54)(1, -2, 7).

deps.name: Find a and other eigenvalues

items.name: Show sum of squared derivatives for cycloid
items.how: For the curve x = a(t - sin t), y = a(1 - cos t) (a > 0), show that (dx/dt)^2 + (dy/dt)^2 = k a^2 sin^2(t/2) with k to be found.
items.ms: B1 at least one correct derivative; M1 square and add using cos^2 + sin^2 = 1 to get an expression in cos t; dM1 replace cos t by 1 - 2sin^2(t/2); A1 4a^2 sin^2(t/2), k = 4.

items.name: Surface area of revolution of cycloid arch
items.how: The curve from t = 0 to t = 2pi is rotated through 2pi about the x-axis; determine the surface area in terms of pi and a, with no calculator-based integration.
items.ms: M1 apply S = 2pi times the integral of y sqrt(...) dt using the part (a) result with a square root giving p sin(t/2); dM1 trig identities to arguments of t/2 only, giving sin^3(t/2); A1ft correct antiderivative -2cos(t/2) + (2/3)cos^3(t/2) times 8 pi a^2; ddM1 limits 0 and 2pi; A1 (64/3) pi a^2.

items.name: Angle between line and plane to nearest degree
items.how: Line l passes through (1, 0, 1) and meets the plane at (1, 2, 3); determine the acute angle between plane and line to the nearest degree.
items.ms: B1 direction of l as (0, 2, 2); M1 scalar product of normal and direction divided by the product of magnitudes; A1ft correct numerical expression (value 0.4029...); A1 awrt 24 degrees (acute angle with the plane is 90 minus the angle to the normal, 66.24). items.name: Reduction formula for integral of cos^n x
items.how: With I_n the integral of cos^n x, prove I_n = (1/n) cos^(n-1)x sin x + ((n-1)/n) I_(n-2) for n >= 2.
items.ms: M1 split cos^n as cos x times cos^(n-1)x; dM1 integrate by parts to p sin x cos^(n-1)x + q integral of cos^(n-2)x sin^2 x; A1 replace sin^2 by 1 - cos^2 to get I_n in terms of I_n and I_(n-2); A1* rearrange to the given result with at least one intermediate step and no bracketing errors.
path: FP3.4.5 - The derivation and use of si

items.name: Foci and directrices of ellipse x^2+9y^2=9
items.how: For the ellipse x^2 + 9y^2 = 9, (i) determine the coordinates of the two foci and (ii) write down the equation of each directrix.
items.ms: M1 b^2 = a^2(1 - e^2) with a = 3, b = 1; A1 e = 2sqrt2/3; B1 foci (+/-2sqrt2, 0); B1ft directrices x = +/-9/(2 sqrt2) = +/-9 sqrt2/4 as single fractions (x = a/e). Not a follow-through mark for the foci.

Using one specific P or just 2a = 6 scores 0.

items.name: Locus of midpoint of chord is line
items.how: The line y = 2x + c through P meets the ellipse again at Q and M is the midpoint of PQ; show that as P varies the locus of M is a straight line through the origin.
items.ms: M1 substitute the line into the ellipse; A1 correct quadratic 37x^2 + 36cx + 9c^2 - 9 = 0; dM1 A1 x-coordinate of M as half the sum of roots (x = -18c/37); ddM1 eliminate c using y = 2x + c to get an equation in x and y only; A1* y = -x/18 with a conclusion that it passes through the origin.

items.name: Two integrals giving arctan and arcsin
items.how: Question text not captured in the input; from the scheme it is two unrelated parts: (i) evaluate exactly a definite integral of 8/(16 + x^2) (limits 4 to 4 sqrt3), (ii) given a definite integral of 2/sqrt(9 - 4x^2) up to an unknown upper limit k has value pi/12, find k.
items.ms: (i) M1 obtains arctan(x/4) form with coefficient 2; dM1 substitute limits and subtract; A1 pi/6. (ii) M1 A1 obtain arcsin(2x/3) (fully correct integration); dM1 substitute limits, set the result equal to pi/12 and solve for k with correct order of operations; A1 k = 3 sqrt2 / 4. Common wrong answer k = 0.913 from mis-integrating the arcsin term.

items.name: Find unknowns in matrix inverse pair

items.name: Cartesian equation of line before transformation

items.name: Foci and directrices in terms of e

items.ms: B1 foci (+/-7e, 0); B1 directrices x = +/-7/e. Special case: consistently using 49 for 7 scores B0 B1.

items.name: Find e from y-intercept
items.how: Given the ellipse crosses the y-axis at (0, +/-4 sqrt3), determine the value of e.
items.ms: M1 replace b^2 by (4 sqrt3)^2 = 48 and solve 48 = 49(1 - e^2) for e^2 or e; A1 e = 1/7 (not +/-).

items.name: Area of triangle OPM

items.name: Prove tanh identity and tanh^n reduction formula
items.how: Single question with an internal chain: (a) use exponential definitions to prove 1 - sech^2 x = tanh^2 x (3 marks); (b) for I_n = integral of tanh^n 3x dx from 0 to (1/3) ln 2, show I_n = I_(n-2) - p^(n-1)/(3(n-1)) with p rational (4 marks); (c) hence find the exact value of the integral of tanh^5 3x over the same limits as a ln b + c (4 marks).
items.ms: (a) B1 replace sech x by 2/(e^x + e^-x); M1 single fraction and expand numerator; A1* reach (e^x - e^-x)^2/(e^x + e^-x)^2. (b) M1 write tanh^n = tanh^(n-2)(1 - sech^2); dM1 integrate tanh^(n-2) 3x sech^2 3x to tanh^(n-1) 3x/(3(n-1)); ddM1 apply limit using tanh(ln 2) = 3/5; A1 p = 3/5. (c) M1 use the reduction formula twice to I_1; M1 integrate tanh 3x to q ln cosh 3x; ddM1 apply the limit with cosh(ln 2) = 5/4; A1 (1/3) ln(5/4) - 177/2500.

items.name: Differentiate arccos(sech x)
items.how: Given y = arccos(sech x) for x > 0, show that dy/dx = sech x.
items.ms: M1 take cos of both sides and differentiate implicitly to get -sin y dy/dx = -sech x tanh x; dM1 use correct identities (sin y = tanh x) to get an equation in x only with no roots; A1* fully correct proof. Clear errors such as treating d/dx(sech x) as +sech x tanh x score A0.

items.name: Minimum point of arccos sech plus coth
items.how: P is the minimum point of y = arccos(sech x) + coth x for x > 0; show that its x-coordinate is ln(q + sqrt(q^2 - 1)) with q involving sqrt k, k an integer.
items.ms: B1 derivative of coth x (-cosech^2 x); M1 set f'(x) = 0 using part (a) and identities to get a 3TQ in cosh x or sech x; A1 cosh^2 x - cosh x - 1 = 0 (or sech form); dM1 solve for an exact value > 1; ddM1 apply the log form of arcosh; A1 x = ln((1 + sqrt5)/2 + sqrt(((1 + sqrt5)/2)^2 - 1)), k = 5. Giving cosh x = (1 + sqrt5)/2 with no source scores B1 M1 A1 dM1 only.

deps.name: Differentiate arccos(sech x)

items.name: Perimeter of region as integral for parabola
items.how: Region R is bounded by y^2 = 8x and the line x = 18; show that the perimeter is alpha + 2 times the integral from 0 to beta of sqrt(1 + y^2/16) dy, with alpha and beta found (all stages of working shown).
items.ms: B1 dx/dy = y/4; M1 form sqrt(1 + (dx/dy)^2) dy correctly; A1 perimeter = 24 + 2 integral from 0 to 12 of sqrt(1 + y^2/16) dy, using y = +/-12 at x = 18 and symmetry about the x-axis.

Column order must match D.

items.name: Differentiate arctan 2x/3 then integrate by parts
items.how: Question text not captured in the input; from the scheme it has two parts: (a) differentiate y = arctan(2x/3) (2 marks), (b) integrate arctan(2x/3) with respect to x (4 marks), using part (a) in the follow-through.
items.ms: (a) M1 derivative of arctan(qx) as p/(1 + (qx)^2) with brackets around qx; A1 6/(9 + 4x^2). (b) M1 integration by parts the correct way round, A1ft using their part (a) result; M1 integrate x/(9 + 4x^2) as a ln term; A1 x arctan(2x/3) - (3/4) ln(9 + 4x^2) + c (the +c is not required).

items.name: Ellipse directrix giving two values of a
items.how: The line x = 9 is a directrix of the ellipse x^2/a^2 + y^2/8 = 1 (a > 0); find the two possible exact values of a (the 8 is taken from the scheme).
items.ms: B1 both equations a/e = 9 and a^2(1 - e^2) = 8; M1 A1 eliminate to a quadratic in a^2 (a^4 - 81a^2 + 648 = 0) or in e^2, with terms collected; M1 solve the quadratic for a^2 or e^2; M1 A1 complete method to a, using a = 9e at least once, giving a = 3 and a = 6 sqrt2. Do not accept +/- unless the negative is rejected.

items.name: Prove cosh^2 - sinh^2 = 1 by exponentials
items.how: Using the definitions of sinh x and cosh x in terms of exponentials, prove cosh^2 x - sinh^2 x = 1.

(b) B1 partial description (e.g. wrong direction), B1 translation of 2 units in the positive x-direction (vector (2, 0)). (c) M1 substitute x = -4 and solve, A1 k = 2. (d) M1 equate and cross-multiply to a quadratic, dM1 solve 2x^2 + 3x - 20 = 0, A1 x = 5/2, A1 Q = (5/2, 12).

items.name: Equation of line from intercepts
items.how: From a sketch, line l cuts the y-axis at -12 and the x-axis at 4; find its equation in the form y = mx + c.
items.ms: M1 for y = mx + c with m or c correct (m = 12/4 = 3 or c = -12), A1 for y = 3x - 12, which needs the 'y ='.
path: Topic 2 Coordinate geometry in the (x, y) plane
P1.2.1 - Equation of a straight line,

items.name: Deduce second root by symmetry
items.how: Quadratic curve C has a minimum point at (7, -18) and cuts the x-axis at 4 and at k; deduce the value of k.
items.ms: B1 for k = 10 (condone x = 10 or (10, 0)), by symmetry about x = 7.

items.name: Find quadratic from roots and minimum
items.how: Find f(x), the quadratic with minimum point (7, -18) that cuts the x-axis at 4 and k.
items.ms: M1 for y = A(x - 4)(x - 10) or y = C(x - 7)^2 - 18, dM1 for using (7, -18) or a root to find A or C, A1 for 2(x - 4)(x - 10) or 2(x - 7)^2 - 18 (the 'y =' is not needed).

deps.name: Deduce second root by symmetry

items.name: Define region using inequalities
items.how: Use inequalities to define the shaded region R, bounded by the line l, the curve C and the y-axis (with x = 4).
items.ms: M1 for two of y >= 3x - 12, y <= 2(x - 4)(x - 10), x >= 0, x <= 4 (follow through their (a) linear and (c) quadratic; 'R' in place of y is not allowed), A1 for all correct with no follow through, e.g. 3x - 12 <= y <= 2(x - 4)(x - 10), 0 <= x <= 4.

deps.name: Equation of line from intercepts
Find quadratic from roots and minimum

items.name: Period of tangent function
items.how: State the period of tan x.
items.ms: B1 for pi radians (180 degrees condoned).
path: P1.3.3 - Sine, cosine and tangent fun

items.name: Count tangent graph roots in intervals
items.how: Using the sketch of y = tan x and the line y = pi*x, write down the number of roots of (i) tan x = (pi + 2)x for -pi < x < pi, (ii) tan x = pi*x for -2pi < x < 2pi, (iii) tan x = pi*x for -100pi < x < 100pi.
items.ms: Three independent B1 marks, no working needed: (i) 3, (ii) 5, (iii) 201. Marks are lost by miscounting the repeated intersections each period or the root at the origin.

deps.name: Period of tangent function

path: P1.3.3 - Sine, cosine and tangent fun

items.name: Sign of factorised cubic from graph
items.how: From the sketch of C: y = f(x) = (3x + 20)(x + 6)(2x - 3), state the values of x for which f(x) > 0.
items.ms: M1 for one of -20/3 < x < -6 or x > 3/2, A1 for both, written as inequalities or interval notation (e.g. -20/3 < f(x) < -6 notation is condoned for M1 only).

items.name: Expand three linear brackets
items.how: Expand (3x + 20)(x + 6)(2x - 3), writing the answer as a polynomial in simplest form.
items.ms: M1 for multiplying two brackets to a quadratic before the third, A1 for 6x^3 + alpha*x^2 + beta*x - 360 (alpha, beta not both zero), A1 for 6x^3 + 67x^2 + 126x - 360. Dividing through (x^3 + 67/6 x^2 + ...) loses the last A.

items.name: Tangent at y-intercept meets curve again
items.how: The line l is the tangent to C at the point where C cuts the y-axis and cuts C again at P; find, using algebra (no calculator technology), the x coordinate of P.
items.ms: M1 differentiate and substitute x = 0 for gradient 126, A1ft l: y = 126x - 360, dM1 set equal to the cubic, ddM1 solve a cubic of the form ax^3 + bx^2 = 0 by taking out x^2, A1 x = -67/6 (x = 0 ignored). An error in the x coefficient of the expansion in (b) can be fully recovered here.

deps.name: Expand three linear brackets

items.name: Normal equation from tangent equation
items.how: Curve C: y = f(x), x > 0 with f''(x) = 4x + x^(-1/2) (index partly lost in the input); P has x coordinate 4 and the tangent at P is y = 3x + 4; find an equation of the normal at P.
items.ms: M1 for stating or implying the normal gradient -1/3, A1 for a correct full equation, e.g. y - 16 = -(1/3)(x - 4); the y coordinate 16 comes from the tangent equation, and (y - 16)/(x - 4) = -1/3 is not accepted as an equation.

items.name: Integrate second derivative twice for f
items.how: Find f(x), in simplest form, given f''(x) = 4x + x^(-1/2), f'(4) = 3 (tangent gradient) and f(4) = 16 (point P).
items.ms: M1 integrate f'' once (one index correct), dM1 use f'(4) = 3 to find the constant -33, A1 f'(x) = 2x^2 + 2x^(1/2) - 33, dM1 integrate again, ddM1 use f(4) = 16 for the second constant, A1 f(x) = (2/3)x^3 + (4/3)x^(3/2) - 33x + 284/3. Work for this part may be seen in (a).

deps.name: Normal equation from tangent equation

path: P1.5.2 - Integration of xn and relate

items.name: Reduce exponential equation to quadratic in p + Solve exponential equation via quadratic
items.how: Hence solve 3*9^x + 3^(x+2) = 1 + 3^(x-1) (non-calculator, all stages).
items.ms: M1 for a valid non-calculator solution of 9p^2 + 26p - 3 = 0 (answers written down score M0), A1 (M1 on e-pen) for 3^x = 1/9 clearly stated as a value of 3^x (3^x = -3 can be ignored), A1 for x = -2 only.

items.name: Radius of sector from area + Angle AOB from straight line + Total area of stage
items.how: Hence find the total area of the stage in m^2 to 1 d.p. (sector plus two triangles with sides 5.77 m and 6.25 m).
items.ms: M1 for the area of triangle AOB = (1/2)(5.77)(6.25)sin(0.37), dM1 for full method 40 + 2*triangle, A1 for awrt 53.1 (53.0 condoned). Degree working is allowed but part (b) must be in radians.
path: P1.3.1 - The sine and cosine rules, a

items.name: Radius of sector from area + Angle AOB from straight line + Total area of stage + Total perimeter of stage
items.how: Hence find the total perimeter of the stage in m to 1 d.p.
items.ms: M1 for the arc length r*theta = 5.77*2.4, M1 for the cosine rule to find AB (or CD), ddM1 for the full perimeter 12.5 + 2AB + arc, A1 for awrt 30.9. Taking AB = 6.25sin(0.37) (right-angle assumption) is a common error giving M1 M0 ddM0 A0.
path: P1.3.1 - The sine and cosine rules, a

items.name: Expand cubic product then integrate
items.how: Single question (stem text missing from the input, reconstructed from the scheme): find the integral of (2x - 5)(3x + 2)(2x + 5) with respect to x.
items.ms: M1 multiply two brackets to a quadratic and then the third, A1 12x^3 + 8x^2 - 75x - 50, M1 integrate with an index raised and processed, A1ft two correct collected terms, A1 3x^4 + (8/3)x^3 - (75/2)x^2 - 50x + c; the +c is required and clearing fractions after a correct answer is not ignored.
path: P1.5.2 - Integration of xn and relate

items.name: Sin of angle from triangle area
items.how: Triangle ABC with AB = 15 cm, AC = 25 cm, angle BAC = theta degrees and area 100 cm^2; find the value of sin(theta).
items.ms: M1 for area = (1/2)ab sin C with the given data (slips condoned), A1 for sin(theta) = 8/15 or an exact equivalent fraction; finishing with sin C = 8/15 is A0 but later marks are still available.
path: P1.3.1 - The sine and cosine rules, a

items.name: Cosine rule with obtuse angle
items.how: Given that theta > 90, find the length of BC in cm to 3 s.f.
items.ms: M1 cosine rule 15^2 + 25^2 - 2(15)(25)cos(angle) using an angle from their part (a), dM1 full cosine rule with the obtuse angle 180 - 32.2, A1 cso awrt 38.5. Using the acute angle (BC about 14.7) loses dM1 and A1; using radians for a degree-labelled angle is a special case M1 dM1 A0.

deps.name: Sin of angle from triangle area

path: P1.3.1 - The sine and cosine rules, a

items.name: Differentiate algebraic fraction as power terms
items.how: Curve C: y = (5x^3 - 8)/(2x^2), x > 0 (reconstructed from the scheme); find dy/dx, giving the answer in simplest form.
items.ms: M1 write y as a sum of two terms with at least one correct index ((5/2)x - 4x^(-2)), dM1 both indices correct and differentiated (Px + Qx^(-2) to A + Bx^(-3)), A1 one correct term, A1 5/2 + 8x^(-3) or 5/2 + 8/x^3. A quotient-rule route is accepted, earning the first two marks together.
path: P1.4.2 - Differentiation of xn, and r

items.name: Tangent equation in integer form
items.how: P(2, 4) lies on C; find an equation of the tangent to C at P in the form ax + by + c = 0 where a, b and c are integers.
items.ms: M1 substitute x = 2 into their dy/dx (not into y) to get the gradient 7/2, M1 y - 4 = m(x - 2) with their numerical gradient (y = mx + c must reach c), A1 7x - 2y - 6 = 0 or any integer multiple. A gradient from a calculator with no working earns only the last M1 A1.

deps.name: Differentiate algebraic fraction as power terms

items.name: Equation of line through two points
items.how: Line l1 passes through P(-2, 9) and Q(10, 6); find its equation in the form y = mx + c (show all stages, no calculator).
items.ms: M1 gradient as change in y over change in x the right way up, dM1 line through a point with their gradient and coordinates in the correct places, A1 y = -(1/4)x + 17/2 in the form y = mx + c. A simultaneous-equation route (9 = -2m + c, 6 = 10m + c) is also accepted.
path: Topic 2 Coordinate geometry in the (x, y) plane
P1.2.1 - Equation of a straight line,

items.name: Foot of perpendicular from origin
items.how: Line l2 passes through the origin O perpendicular to l1 and meets l1 at R; find the coordinates of R (non-calculator, show stages).
items.ms: B1ft l2: y = 4x (negative reciprocal of their gradient), M1 solve their l2 and l1 simultaneously by a non-calculator route (some working visible), A1 one correct coordinate, A1 R = (2, 8). Answers with no or insufficient working lose marks.

deps.name: Equation of line through two points

path: Topic 2 Coordinate geometry in the (x, y) plane

items.name: Exact area of triangle OPQ
items.how: Find the exact area of triangle OPQ (non-calculator; surds expected).
items.ms: M1 length OR (or PQ) by Pythagoras from coordinates, dM1 full area (1/2)*OR*PQ, A1 51 with relevant surd working seen, e.g. (1/2)*2root17*3root17; decimal work or unexplained 153 and 68 do not earn the A. Alternatives: shoelace, trapezium minus two right triangles, cosine rule.

deps.name: Foot of perpendicular from origin

path: Topic 2 Coordinate geometry in the (x, y) plane

items.name: Minimum point of cosine graph
items.how: From the graph of y = 5cos(x) (x in degrees), state the coordinates of the minimum point P.
items.ms: B1 for one correct coordinate, B1 for both: P = (540, -5). Swapped coordinates, radians (withhold a mark once) or unbracketed coordinates lose marks.
path: P1.3.3 - Sine, cosine and tangent fun

items.name: Maximum point of transformed cosine curves
items.how: Find the coordinates of the maximum point with smallest x > 0 on (i) y = 5cos(x) - 2 and (ii) y = -5cos(x).
items.ms: (i) B1 B1 for (360, 3); (ii) B1 B1 for (180, 5); one mark per correct coordinate (B0 B1 is not possible). Flipped coordinates earn B1 B0; radians or missing brackets cost a mark the first time.
path: P1.3.3 - Sine, cosine and tangent fun

items.name: Reciprocal curve sketch and line non-intersection
items.how: (a) Sketch y = 4/(x - k), k > 0, showing axis intercepts and the vertical asymptote; (b) given that the line y = 9 - x does not cross or touch the curve, find the range of values of k.
items.ms: (a) M1 decreasing branch in quadrant 1, A1 correct shape and position (quadrants 1, 3 and 4), B1 y-intercept (0, -4/k) on the negative y-axis, B1 asymptote x = k. (b) M1 equate to form a quadratic, A1 x^2 - (9 + k)x + 9k + 4 = 0, dM1 discriminant < 0, ddM1 solve k^2 - 18k + 65 and take the inside region, A1 cso 5 < k < 13 (not the outside region).

items.name: Show length AO using arc length
items.how: Platform made of sector DOC and a larger-angle sector AOBEA, both centre O: angle AOB = 0.8 rad, arc CD = 9 m, DA : AO = 3 : 5; show that AO = 7.03 m to 3 s.f.
items.ms: M1 s = r*theta with s = 9, theta = 0.8, A1 OD = 11.25, A1* AO = (5/8)(11.25) = 7.03 with the method visible (7.03125 may be used later). Show-that: the method must be explicit.

items.name: Perimeter of compound sector platform
items.how: Find the perimeter of the platform in m to 3 s.f.
items.ms: M1 major arc AEB = 7.03(2pi - 0.8) (about 38.6), M1 add the pieces 9 + 2(11.25 - 7.03) + arc AEB, A1 awrt 56.0 (56 condoned after correct working).

deps.name: Show length AO using arc length

items.name: Area of compound sector platform
items.how: Find the total area of the platform, in m^2, to the nearest whole number.
items.ms: M1 one sector area ((1/2)(11.25)^2(0.8) = 50.6 or (1/2)(7.03)^2(2pi - 0.8) = 135.4), dM1 add the two sectors, A1 awrt 186.

deps.name: Show length AO using arc length

items.name: Sketch quadratic with given maximum
items.how: C1: y = f(x) is a quadratic with maximum turning point (2, 20) passing through the origin; sketch C1 showing where it cuts the coordinate axes.
items.ms: B1 for an n-shaped quadratic through the origin (quadrants 3, 1 and 4), B1 for the second x-intercept (4, 0) marked on the positive x-axis ((0, 4) is B0).

items.name: Find quadratic from turning point
items.how: Find an expression for f(x), the quadratic with maximum (2, 20) through the origin.
items.ms: M1 form y = Ax(x - 4) or 20 - C(x - 2)^2 (or three equations in ax^2 + bx + c), dM1 find A or C from a given point, A1 -5x(x - 4) = -5x^2 + 20x or 20 - 5(x - 2)^2; may be seen in (c).

deps.name: Sketch quadratic with given maximum

items.name: Intersection of cubic and quadratic
items.how: C2: y = x(x^2 - 4) meets C1 at the origin, P and Q (P has negative x coordinate); using algebra and showing all stages, find the coordinates of P.
items.ms: M1 set x(x^2 - 4) equal to their quadratic through the origin, dM1 expand to px^3 + qx^2 + rx = 0 and take out the factor x, ddM1 solve the quadratic x^2 + 5x - 24 = 0 (calculator allowed), A1 x = -8 chosen (0 and 3 rejected), A1 P = (-8, -480). All stages are required so omissions are penalised.

deps.name: Find quadratic from turning point

items.name: Find k from second derivative zero
items.how: Show all stages: curve C: y = f(x), x > 0 passes through P(2, 8root2), f'(x) = 4x^(3/2) + k/x^2 (reconstructed from the scheme) and f''(x) = 0 at P; find the exact value of k.
items.ms: M1 differentiate f' with at least one index correct, A1 f''(x) = 6x^(1/2) - 2k*x^(-3), dM1 set f''(2) = 0 and solve for k, A1 k = 24root2 (exact). Integrating in (a) or differentiating in (b) earns nothing.
path: P1.4.2 - Differentiation of xn, and r

items.name: Integrate to find f using point
items.how: Find f(x), giving the answer in simplest form, using f'(x) with your value of k and the point P(2, 8root2).
items.ms: M1 integrate f' with one index correct, A1ft (8/5)x^(5/2) - k*x^(-1) (follow through their k), dM1 use P to find c as a multiple of root2, A1 f(x) = (8/5)x^(5/2) - 24root2/x + 68root2/5 or any simplified equivalent.

deps.name: Find k from second derivative zero

path: P1.5.2 - Integration of xn and relate

items.name: Reduce exponential equation to quadratic in p + Solve exponential equation via quadratic
items.how: Hence solve 2*4^x - 2^(x+3) = 17*2^(x-1) - 4 (non-calculator).
items.ms: M1 for a valid non-calculator solution of 4p^2 - 33p + 8 = 0 with working shown ((4p - 1)(p - 8)), M1 for solving 2^x = k for x (logs allowed if k is not a power of 2), A1 for both x = -2 and x = 3. Roots written straight from a calculator score M0.

items.name: Differentiate power terms and find tangent
items.how: Single question (stem text missing from the input): (a) differentiate a curve given as power terms with fractional and negative indices; (b) find the equation of the tangent at the point where x = 4.
items.ms: (a) M1 reduce a correct power by one, A1 one correct simplified term, A1 dy/dx = (3/8)x^2 + 12x^(-3/2) or equivalent (isw). (b) M1 substitute x = 4 into their derivative (gradient 7.5), M1 tangent through the point at x = 4 with their numerical gradient (y = mx + c must reach c), A1 y = 7.5x - 33. A gradient found by calculator with no working still allows the last two marks.

items.name: Integrate quotient with square root
items.how: Find the integral of (4x^2 + 1)/(2*root x) with respect to x, giving the answer in its simplest form.
items.ms: M1 write as a sum of two terms with an index processed, A1 2x^(3/2) + (1/2)x^(-1/2), M1 raise a correct index by one, A1 one correct simplified term, A1 (4/5)x^(5/2) + x^(1/2) + c (the +c is needed; unprocessed indices lose marks).
path: P1.5.2 - Integration of xn and relate

items.name: Area of major sector
items.how: Shape ABCDA is a sector ABCOA (radius 6 cm, with angle AOD = 0.7 rad removed) joined to a triangle AOD; find the area of the sector to 1 d.p.
items.ms: M1 use (1/2)r^2*theta with r = 6 and any allowable angle, M1 correct attempt with the reflex angle 2pi - 0.7 (awrt 100 or 101 accepted for this mark), A1 awrt 100.5. A degree method is allowed if the angle is awrt 40 or 320.

items.name: Normal to curve from derivative
items.how: Curve y = f(x), x > 0 passes through P(4, 1) with f'(x) = 4x^(1/2) - 2 - 8/(3x^2) (reconstructed from the scheme); find the equation of the normal at P in the form ax + by + c = 0 with integer a, b, c.
items.ms: M1 substitute x = 4 into f'(x) (value 35/6), dM1 perpendicular gradient -6/35, M1 normal through (4, 1) with the changed gradient (one sign slip condoned), A1 6x + 35y - 59 = 0 (any positive integer multiple).

items.name: Integrate derivative to find f
items.how: Find f(x) from f'(x) and the point P(4, 1) on the curve.
items.ms: M1 raise a correct index by one (processed), A1 any two terms correct, A1 all three simplified (8/3)x^(3/2) - 2x + 8/(3x), dM1 substitute x = 4, y = 1 to find c, A1 f(x) = (8/3)x^(3/2) - 2x + 8/(3x) - 13. Differentiating f'(x) in (a) and integrating back in (b) earns nothing.
path: P1.5.2 - Integration of xn and relate

items.name: Minimum point of 4 sin
items.how: State the coordinates of the minimum point of y = 4 sin(theta) for 0 <= theta <= 360 degrees (Figure 3 shows the graph).
items.ms: B1 for either coordinate correct (270 or -4, swapped order condoned for this mark), B1 for (270, -4) with or without the degree symbol.
path: P1.3.3 - Sine, cosine and tangent fun

items.name: Point where cubic touches x-axis
items.how: Curve y = f(x) with f(x) = (x - 4)(2x + 1)^2 (as reconstructed from the scheme) touches the x-axis at P and crosses at Q; state the coordinates of P.
items.ms: B1 for P = (-1/2, 0), the repeated root. If both (4, 0) and (-1/2, 0) are given, P must be identified.

items.name: Horizontal translation through the origin
items.how: The curve y = f(x + a), a a constant, passes through the origin; state the possible values of a.
items.ms: B1 for one correct value (f(a) = 0, so a is an x-intercept of f), B1 for both a = -1/2 and a = 4 and no others, given as values (not 'x = ...'). Writing y = f(x - 1/2) or y = f(x + 4) implies the first mark only.

deps.name: Point where cubic touches x-axis

path: P1.1.12 - Knowledge of the effect of s

items.name: Rationalise denominator with surd + Solve linear equation with surd coefficients
items.how: Hence, or otherwise, solve 4x = 2root2*x + 20root2, giving x in the form p + q*root2 with p and q rational.
items.ms: M1 collect the x terms on one side and the constant on the other, dM1 x = 20root2 times the result of (a) (i.e. dividing by 4 - 2root2), A1 10root2 + 10 (10 + 10root2); the A1 cannot be earned without the use of the part (a) value. Squaring or repeating the rationalisation are accepted alternatives with the same marks.
path: P1.1.2 - Use and manipulation of surd

items.name: Perimeter inequality for garden + Area inequality leading to quadratic + Combine inequalities for range of x
items.how: Hence state the range of possible values of x.
items.ms: B1 for 1.5 < x < 2 (or x > 1.5 and x < 2); 'or' between the two inequalities is B0.
path: P1.1.9 - Solutions of linear and quad

items.name: Solve cubic by factorising out x + Solve higher-power equation by substitution
items.how: Hence find all real solutions of an equation of the same form as (a) in terms of (y - 5), with even powers (y - 5)^6, (y - 5)^4 and (y - 5)^2 as read from the scheme.
items.ms: B1 y = 5 stated as a solution, M1 recognise (y - 5)^2 equals a positive root from (a) (7/2) and solve for y, A1ft one solution of the form 5 +/- root(7/2) (decimals allowed for this mark only), A1 both 5 + root(7/2) and 5 - root(7/2) in exact form, no complex or extra solutions.

items.name: Tangency condition gives constant c + Point of tangency coordinates
items.how: Hence find the coordinates of the point of intersection.
items.ms: M1 solve the quadratic x^2 - 7x - c = 0 with their c (a repeated root x = 7/2), dM1 find y for their x, A1 (7/2, 7/4). A correct answer with correct c scores all three marks if no incorrect working is seen.

items.name: Obtuse angle by sine rule + Perimeter of sector and triangle shape
items.how: Hence find the perimeter of shape ABCDA to 1 d.p.
items.ms: M1 arc ABC = 6(2pi - 0.7) = 33.50, M1 length OD by the sine rule with angle OAD = 0.7 subtracted from pi less 2.258 (or the cosine rule and a quadratic in OD), giving about 1.42, ddM1 perimeter 33.50 + 5 + (6 - 1.42), A1 awrt 43.1.

items.name: Sketch 1 + sin and tan curves + Count solutions of trig equation graphically
items.how: Hence find the number of solutions of tan(theta) = 1 + sin(theta) in (i) a long interval (a whole number of 360 degree periods) and (ii) a second interval that omits part of the first.
items.ms: (i) M1 for the number of intersections per period (2) times the number of periods (6), A1 12; (ii) B1ft 11, or a follow-through of their (i) minus the solutions in the omitted section. If graphs are missing, 12 and 11 still earn their marks.
path: P1.3.3 - Sine, cosine and tangent fun

items.name: Expand cubic and differentiate + Show horizontal tangent at stationary point
items.how: Hence show that the equation of the tangent to the curve where x = 2.5 can be expressed in the form y = k, and find k.
items.ms: M1 evaluate f'(2.5) for their f', A1 show f'(2.5) = 12(2.5)^2 - 24(2.5) - 15 = 0 with embedded values (needs a correct f'), A1 cso y coordinate -54 so the tangent is y = -54. Solving f'(x) = 0 to get x = -0.5 and 2.5 is accepted for the first two marks.

items.name: Differentiate power terms and find normal
items.how: Single question (stem text missing from the input): (a) differentiate a curve given as power terms (x^2, x^(-1/2), x^(-1) and a constant); (b) find the equation of the normal at the point (4, 3) in the form ax + by + c = 0.
items.ms: (a) M1 reduce the power on any term (constant to 0), then A1 A1 A1 for one, two, then all three terms of dy/dx = (2/3)x - 2x^(-3/2) - (8/3)x^(-2) (no isw in this part). (b) M1 substitute x = 4 into their derivative (9/4), M1 perpendicular gradient -4/9, dM1 line through (4, 3) with the changed gradient (y = mx + c must reach c), A1 4x + 9y - 43 = 0 or an integer multiple.

items.name: Show relation using cosine rule
items.how: Triangle ABC with AB = p m, AC = q m, BC = 2root2 m and angle BAC = 60 degrees; show that p^2 + q^2 - pq = 8 (all stages).
items.ms: M1 cosine rule (2root2)^2 = p^2 + q^2 - 2pq*cos60 (or a perpendicular from B giving two right triangles), A1* the given result with cos60 replaced by 1/2 and no bracket errors; stating = 8 without any working scores no A mark.
path: P1.3.1 - The sine and cosine rules, a

items.name: Integrate product over root term
items.how: Find the integral of (3x + 2)(root x - 5)/(4*root x) with respect to x (stem partly lost in the input, reconstructed from the scheme), writing each term in simplest form.

items.ms: M1 relate dx and du (x = ((u - 3)^2 + 1)/2 so dx = (u - 3)du); A1 dx/du = u - 3; M1 write the whole integral in u; dM1 divide to A + B/u (4 - 12/u); ddM1 integrate to Au + B ln u; A1ft 4u - 12 ln u; M1 apply limits (u = 4 to 8, or revert to x with 1 to 13); A1 16 - 12 ln 2.

items.name: Implicit differentiation with product rule

items.name: Normal at second y-axis intercept

items.ms: B1 y = 3/2 at x = 0 for P (ignore y = 0); M1 substitute x = 0 and their y into their dy/dx for a numerical gradient (-7/2); dM1 negative reciprocal for the normal and form the equation; A1 y = (2/7)x + 3/2. Using (0, 0) for P loses the last three marks.

deps.name: Implicit differentiation with product rule

items.name: Integrate e^2x sin x by parts twice

Three equivalent set-ups are credited.

items.name: Prove lines are skew when b not 7
items.how: Lines l1: r = (-1, 5, 4) + lambda(2, -1, 5) and l2: r = (2, -2, -5) + mu(4, -3, b); prove that for all b not equal to 7 the lines are skew.
items.ms: M1 equate and solve two component equations for lambda or mu; dM1 find both; A1 mu = -11/2, lambda = -19/2; ddM1 substitute into the third equation to get a condition on b; A1 lines intersect only when b = 7; A1* cso state they meet only when b = 7 and are not parallel, so skew for b not equal to 7.

items.name: Partial fractions then separable water-depth model

items.ms: (a) M1 method for a constant, A1 one correct, A1 (1/8)(1/(H - 5) - 1/(H + 3)). (b) M1 separate variables and use (a); M1 integrate to ln terms; A1ft; M1 use H = 13, t = 0 to find c; A1 correct equation in H and t; dddM1 make H the subject; A1* given result. (c) M1 set expression = 8 to get e^(-0.2t) = 6/11; dM1 log work; A1 t = awrt 3.03 days. (d) B1 k = 5.

items.ms: M1 integrate to at least one ln term; M1 the (2x + 1)^(-2) term integrates to K/(2x + 1); A1ft (2/5)ln(x - 2) - (2/5)ln(2x + 1) + 1/(2(2x + 1)) following through on their constants; dM1 substitute the limits and subtract; M1 combine to a single ln using a log law; A1 (2/5)ln(6/5) - 1/75 or equivalent.

items.name: Binomial (1 + kx)^(1/2) coefficients and approximation
items.how: Single question whose stem was not extracted; from the mark scheme: the expansion of (1 + kx)^(1/2) begins 1 + x/8 + A x^2 + B x^3; (a)(i) find k, (ii) find A and B (5 marks); (b) substitute x = 0.6 to approximate sqrt(1.15) (2 marks).
items.ms: (a)(i) M1 equate the x coefficient k/2 = 1/8, A1 k = 1/4. (ii) M1 correct third or fourth term using their k; A1 A = -1/128; A1 B = 1/1024. (b) M1 substitute x = 0.6 (kx = 0.15) into the expansion; A1 1.072398 to 6 decimal places.

items.name: Volume of revolution of region above curve
items.how: Region R (Figure 1) is bounded by the curve y = 9/(2x - 3)^1.25 (form from the scheme), the line y = 9 and the line x = 6; it is rotated through 2 pi about the x-axis; find the exact volume by algebraic integration.
items.ms: B1 lower limit x = 2 (where the curve meets y = 9); M1 integrate y^2 = 81/(2x - 3)^2.5; A1 -27/(2x - 3)^1.5 times the factor (alpha) used; dM1 apply limits 2 and 6 for the solid under the curve (26 pi); A1 26 pi; ddM1 subtract from the cylinder, pi x 9^2 x (6 - 2) - 26 pi; A1 298 pi.
path: P4.6.1 - Evaluation of volume of revo

items.name: Time to fill bowl at constant inflow
items.how: A bowl of height 20 cm has water volume V = (1/3)h^2(h + 4) at depth h; water flows in at 160 cm^3/s; find the time taken to fill the bowl.
items.ms: M1 find V at h = 20 from the formula and divide by 160; A1 20 seconds (units required).

items.name: Rate of change of water depth at h = 5
items.how: Find, according to the model, the rate of change of the depth of the water in cm/s when h = 5.
items.ms: M1 differentiate V (expand or product rule) to alpha h^2 + beta h; M1 chain rule dV/dt = dV/dh x dh/dt with dV/dt = 160; A1 correct equation 160 = (h^2 + 8h/3) dh/dt; dM1 substitute h = 5 and solve for dh/dt; A1 96/23 or awrt 4.2 cm/s.

items.name: Substitution u = sqrt(x) then partial fractions
items.how: Use algebraic integration and u = sqrt(x) to find the exact value of the integral of 10/(5x + 2x sqrt(x)) dx (limits 1 to 4 in the scheme), written as 4 ln(a/b) with integers a and b; calculator-only solutions not acceptable.
items.ms: B1 dx/du = 2u; M1 write all terms in u including dx; A1 20/(5u + 2u^2) du; dM1 partial fractions; A1 4/u - 8/(5 + 2u); ddM1 integrate to ln u and ln(5 + 2u) terms; M1 apply limits u = 1 to 2 (or x = 1 to 4); A1 4 ln(14/9).

items.name: Show dy/dx for y^2 = y e^-2x - 3x
items.how: Curve y^2 = y e^(-2x) - 3x; show that dy/dx = (2y e^(-2x) + 3)/(e^(-2x) - 2y).
items.ms: B1 differentiate y^2 to 2y dy/dx; M1 product rule on y e^(-2x); A1 correct 2y dy/dx = e^(-2x) dy/dx - 2y e^(-2x) - 3; A1* rearrange via a line equivalent to (e^(-2x) - 2y) dy/dx = 2y e^(-2x) + 3 with correct bracketing.

items.name: Intersection of two tangents at y-axis points
items.how: The curve crosses the y-axis at the origin and at P; the tangents at the origin and at P meet at R; find the coordinates of R.
items.ms: B1 P = (0, 1) from y^2 = y at x = 0; M1 attempt a tangent at (0,0) or P using the (a) gradient; A1 y = 3x or y = -5x + 1; dM1 both tangents and solve simultaneously; A1 R = (1/8, 3/8).

items.name: Collinear points vectors and contradiction proof
items.how: Two unrelated parts: (i) A, B, C are collinear with B between A and C and AB : AC = 1 : 3; show c = 3b - 2a for their position vectors (3 marks); (ii) for integer n, prove by contradiction that if n^2 is a multiple of 3 then n is a multiple of 3 (5).
items.ms: (i) M1 two of AB, AC, BC by subtraction; dM1 use the ratio (e.g. BC = 2AB or AC = 3AB); A1* expand and reach c = 3b - 2a. (ii) B1 assume n is not a multiple of 3 yet n^2 is; M1 write n = 3p + 1 or 3p + 2 and square; M1 expand both cases; A1 show each is not a multiple of 3 (9p^2 + 6p + 1 and 9p^2 + 12p + 4 with reasons); A1 minimal conclusion. B0 M1 M1 M1 A1 is possible.

items.name: Binomial expansion and coefficient condition for k

items.ms: (a) B1 A = 1/9; (b) B1 correct unsimplified x and x^2 coefficients from 3^-2(1 + kx/3)^-2, M1 sets x^2 coefficient equal to 3 times the x coefficient to get a two-term quadratic in k, A1* k^2 + 6k = 0; (c)(i) B1 k = -6 only (k = 0 rejected), (ii) M1 A1 x^3 coefficient 32/9 using (-2)(-3)(-4)/3! (k/3)^3 and the 3^-2 factor. Marks are lost for dropping the 3^-2 factor or the brackets on (k/3)^2, and for not rejecting k = 0.

items.name: Partial fractions then separable differential equation
items.how: (a) Express 1/((1 + 3x)(1 - x)) in partial fractions; (b) Hence find the particular solution of (1 + 3x)(1 - x) dy/dx = tan y, given an initial condition, in the form sin^n y = f(x) with n to be found.
items.ms: (a) B1 identity 1 = A(1 - x) + B(1 + 3x), M1 finds A or B, A1 3/(4(1 + 3x)) + 1/(4(1 - x)). (b) M1 separates to integrate cot y dy, M1 integrates the partial fractions to ln terms, A1ft ln sin y = (1/4)ln(1 + 3x) - (1/4)ln(1 - x) (+c), dM1 uses the initial condition for c, M1 log work to sin^n y form, A1 sin^4 y = (1 + 3x)/(5(1 - x)). Common losses: not integrating cot y to ln sin y, sign errors on the (1 - x) term, omitting c.

items.name: Proof by contradiction n squared minus 2
items.how: Use proof by contradiction to show that n^2 - 2 is never divisible by 4 when n is an integer.
items.ms: M1 sets up an algebraic statement such as n^2 - 2 = 4k (assumption), A1 n^2 = 4k + 2 = 2(2k + 1), dM1 complete argument leading to a contradiction (n^2 even so n even so n^2 a multiple of 4, but n^2 - 2 then cannot be a multiple of 4), A1* contradiction drawn and conclusion stated; an initial assumption must be present. Alternatives using n = 2m and n = 2m + 1 (4m^2 - 2, 4(m^2 + m) - 1) are accepted.

items.name: Vector equation of line through two points + Perpendicular vectors find p + Area of right-angled triangle ABC

items.name: Integration by parts and by substitution

(ii) B1 substitution and differential (u = 2x-1 most common), M1 integrand fully in u, A1 correct integrand, dM1 integrate to p ln u + q/u form, A1 correct integration, M1 changed limits (or back-substitute), A1 3/20 + ln 4; avoiding substitution scores the special case B0M0A0 then M1A1dM1A1.

items.name: Contradiction proof that k + 9/k >= 6

(b) B1 for a negative value such as k = -3 giving -6, with a minimal conclusion; arguments about k = 0 are not credited.

items.ms: B1 for t = 2 from setting the j component to zero; M1A1 for differentiating the velocity to get a = -6t i - 3t^2 j; M1A1 for substituting their t and using Pythagoras (sqrt288 = 17.0). Marks are lost by using t = 0 or by not square-rooting.
path: Topic 1 Kinematics of a particle moving in a straight line or plane

items.name: Position vector by integrating velocity
items.how: Find the position vector of P at t = 3, given the velocity function and that r = -5i + 2j when t = 1.
items.ms: M1A1 for integrating the velocity (powers up by 1, i and j kept); M1A1 for using t = 1 and -5i + 2j to find the constant vector and a complete expression for r; A1 for the final position vector at t = 3 (23i - 2j). Marks are lost by omitting the constant of integration.
path: Topic 1 Kinematics of a particle moving in a straight line or plane

items.name: Composite wire and particles suspended from vertex
items.how: Find the angle between AB and the vertical when a uniform wire right-angled triangle (3a, 4a, 5a sides) with particles at B and C hangs freely from A.
items.ms: B1 for total mass 17m; M1A1A1 for a moments equation about AB (wire sides as masses 4m and 5m at their midpoints plus the particle at C) giving x = 30a/17; M1A1A1 for the same about BC giving y = 12a/17; M1A1ft for tan(theta) = x/(3a - y) and A1 for 38 degrees. Marks are lost by treating the wire's centre of mass as the triangle centroid, which caps the mark at B1M0M0M1A1ftA0.

items.name: Work-energy up rough slope to show distance
items.how: Show that d = 2.7 (2 s.f.) using the work-energy principle for a 6.5 kg particle projected up a rough incline at 6 m/s, with the slope given by a tan value and a given coefficient of friction.
items.ms: B1 for R = 6.5g cos(theta) = 6g; M1 for F = mu R; M1 for a work-energy equation with KE, PE and friction work terms; A2 ft (-1 each error); dM1 to solve for d; A1 for the given answer 2.7. No marks are given for a non-energy method.

items.name: Speed on return through starting point
items.how: Find the speed of P as it passes X after sliding back down the plane from rest at Y.
items.ms: M1 for a work-energy equation with the KE terms and 2 x friction work (or KE, PE and friction work from Y), A2 (-1 each error), A1 for 2 m/s. Alternatives are F = ma with v^2 = u^2 + 2as. Marks are lost by giving inaccurate answers such as 2.01 or 2.02.

items.name: Show impulse magnitude in direct collision

items.ms: M1A1 for conservation of linear momentum, M1A1 for Newton's law of restitution the correct way up, M1A1 for solving for the speed of B (4u/7), and A1 for the impulse (4m x 4u/7 = 16mu/7), fully justified. Marks are lost through sign errors or showing too little working for a given answer.

items.ms: (a) M1 differentiate r (both components), A1 correct v, DM1 equate the i component of v to zero and solve for t, A1 v as a vector, about 19.8j m/s (answer must be a vector); (b) M1 differentiate their v (both components), A1 correct a, A1 a evaluated as a vector (isw).

items.name: Acceleration under constant power on level road
items.how: Using the model, find the acceleration of a cyclist (total mass 80 kg, 500 W, constant 60 N resistance) at 6 m/s on a horizontal road.
items.ms: M1 P = Fv (F = 500/6); M1 equation of motion F - 60 = 80a; A1 correct unsimplified equation in F; A1 a = 7/24 (0.29 or better) m s^-2.

items.name: Total work done by cyclist up hill
items.how: Find the total work done by the cyclist from A to B (20 km up a slope rising 300 m, starting from rest and ending at 8 m/s) with a constant 60 N non-gravitational resistance.
items.ms: B1 B1 gain in KE (1/2 x 80 x 8^2) and gain in GPE (80 x 9.8 x 300), one mark per correct term; M1 combined work-energy expression with all terms and no double counting (suvat with F = ma scores M0); A1 correct unsimplified expression including work against resistance 60 x 20000; A1 about 1440 kJ (1400 kJ); joules accepted.

items.name: Power for constant speed uphill
items.how: Find P, the constant power needed for the cyclist to climb a slope (sin(alpha) = 1/20 in the scheme) at a steady 7 m/s with 60 N non-gravitational resistance.
items.ms: M1 equation of motion along the slope with the driving force, 60 N and 80g sin(alpha) (zero resultant); A1 unsimplified equation in P or F with at most one error; A1 correct unsimplified equation in P using F = P/7; A1 P = 694 (690) W.

items.name: Tension in string by moments about hinge
items.how: Show that T = 6W/5, the tension in a string holding a uniform rod AB (weight W, hinged at A, a particle attached at B) in equilibrium; the weight of the particle appears as W/4 in the scheme.
items.ms: M1 moments about A with all terms and forces resolved (M0 if no resolving); A1 correct unsimplified equation; A1* T = 6W/5 with cancelling or simplification shown.

items.name: Magnitude of hinge force on rod
items.how: Find, in terms of W, the magnitude of the force exerted on the rod by the hinge at A.
items.ms: Two independent equations (resolve horizontally and vertically, or moments about B or C, or along/perpendicular to the rod): M1 A1 for the first and M1 A1 for the second, e.g. H = T cos 30, V + T cos 60 = rod and particle weights; DM1 Pythagoras for R; A1 R = (sqrt(601)/20)W, about 1.2W.

items.name: Position, acceleration and timing from velocity vector
items.how: Three-part vector kinematics question (question text missing from the input; reconstructed from the scheme): given v(t) and the position r = -30i - 45j at t = 0, (a) find r at t = 3, (b) find the magnitude of the acceleration at t = 3, (c) find the time T at which a stated ratio of the i and j components of velocity holds.
items.ms: (a) M1 integrate v, A1 correct integration, DM1 use the initial position to find the constant (or a definite integral) and substitute t = 3, A1 r = 87i + 45j; (b) M1 differentiate v, A1 a = (6t + 12)i + (10t + 10)j, DM1 substitute t = 3 and use Pythagoras, A1 50 m s^-2; (c) M1 equation in T from the ratio of components of v, A1 T = 6/7 (0.86).

items.name: Impulse and kinetic energy change give velocity
items.how: Find, in terms of i and j, the velocity of a 3 kg particle after it receives an impulse of magnitude 3 sqrt(82) when moving at 5i, given the new velocity is xi + yj with x, y > 0 and the kinetic energy gained is 138 J.
items.ms: M1 A1 impulse = change in momentum as a vector (3(x - 5)i + 3yj); M1 Pythagoras with |I|^2 = 9 x 82; M1 A1 change in KE 1/2 x 3(x^2 + y^2 - 25) = 138; DM1 solve the simultaneous equations; A1 v = 6i + 9j (A0 for poor notation or subtraction the wrong way round).

items.how: Hence show 3 cot 2t - 14 = 6 sin^2 t cot 2t + 4 sin t cos t can be written 5 sin^2 2t + 14 sin 2t - 3 = 0.
items.ms: M1 use the (a) expression in the equation and multiply by sin 2t, M1 cancel 3cos 2t from both sides and use sin^2 + cos^2 = 1 to a three-term quadratic in sin 2t, A1* the given equation with no errors or invisible brackets.
path: P3.2.3 - Knowledge and use of double

items.name: Rewrite expression in sin2theta and cos2theta only + Show quadratic in sin2theta from trig equation + Solve quadratic in sin2x for x
items.how: Hence solve 3 cot 2x - 14 = 6 sin^2 x cot 2x + 4 sin x cos x for 0 < x < 90 degrees, answers to 1 dp.
items.ms: M1 solve the quadratic (sin 2x = 1/5; -3 rejected) and use arcsin to a value of x, A1 awrt 5.8 or 84.2, A1 both 5.8 and 84.2 with no others in range (sin 2x = 1/5 must be seen).

items.name: Implicit differentiation with given gradient points
items.how: Show all stages: for the curve 4x^2 - y^2 + 2xy + 5 = 0 (powers inferred from the mark scheme), dy/dx = 2 at two points P and Q; find their coordinates.
items.ms: M1 differentiate implicitly, B1 d(2xy)/dx = 2x dy/dx + 2y, A1 8x - 2y dy/dx + 2x dy/dx + 2y = 0, M1 set dy/dx = 2 to get y = 6x, dM1 substitute into the curve to a two-term quadratic (20x^2 = 5), A1 one correct pair, A1 (1/2, 3) and (-1/2, -3); unpaired coordinates or extra solutions lose the last A.

items.name: Partial fractions with division then integrate
items.how: Show all stages: integrate (3x^2 + 8)/(x^2 - 4x) from 1 to 3, giving the answer as a + b ln 3 (limits inferred from the mark scheme).
items.ms: M1 A1 partial fractions A/x + B/(x - 4) with -2 and 14, B1ft the improper fraction written as 3 - 2/x + 14/(x - 4), M1 A1ft integrate to 3x - 2 ln x + 14 ln|x - 4|, dM1 limits and simplify to P + Q ln 3, A1 6 - 16 ln 3. Treating the fraction as proper loses the B1 and later marks.

items.name: Lines meeting and perpendicular, find a, b, c
items.how: Lines l1 and l2 (r = point + parameter x direction, l2 with direction (a, b, -2)) meet when lambda = -2 and are perpendicular; find a, b and c.
items.ms: B1 point of intersection (6, -1, -5) or mu = 4, M1 use the i component to find a, A1 a = -1, dM1 scalar product of directions = 0 (with (-2, 1, 4)) to find b = 6, ddM1 use the j component for c, A1 b = 6, c = -25. Misreading lambda = -2 as 2 loses most marks.

items.name: Coordinates of point at given parameter
items.how: Curve C: x = 8cos^3 t, y = 6 sin^2 t for 0 <= t <= pi/2 (powers inferred from the mark scheme) and P has parameter pi/3; find the coordinates of P.
items.ms: B1 one coordinate and B1 both: P = (1, 4.5) (or 9/2).
path: Topic 3 Coordinate geometry in the (x, y) plane

items.name: Equation of normal to parametric curve
items.how: Find the normal to C at P in the form y = mx + c, showing all stages.
items.ms: M1 A1 dy/dx = (dy/dt)/(dx/dt) = -1/(2cos t) (12 sin t cos t over -24 cos^2 t sin t), dM1 substitute t = pi/3 to get -1, ddM1 negative reciprocal and the line through (1, 4.5), A1 y = x + 3.5. A Cartesian-equation route is an accepted alternative.

items.name: Factorise then prove no integer solutions
items.how: (a) Factorise 4p^2 - q^2; (b) hence prove by contradiction that there are no positive integers p and q with 4p^2 - q^2 = 46 (the squares are inferred from the mark scheme).
items.ms: (a) B1 (2p + q)(2p - q). (b) M1 one valid factor pair (46 and 1, or 23 and 2), A1 correctly solve one pair (p = 11.75 or 6.25), dM1 state and solve both pairs, A1* full proof: assume integers exist, both pairs fail, conclusion. Parity arguments are accepted alternatives.

items.name: Position vector of fourth vertex of parallelogram
items.how: ABCD is a parallelogram with a = i + j - 2k, b = 3i - j + 6k, c = -i + 3j + 6k; find the position vector d.
items.ms: M1 find BA (a - b) or BC (c - b), dM1 d = a - b + c (or c + CD), A1 -3i + 5j - 2k. One correct component alone scores M1 dM1 A0.

items.name: Angle between sides of parallelogram
items.how: Find the angle between the sides AB and BC of the parallelogram.
items.ms: M1 vectors BA = (-2, 2, -8) and BC = (-4, 4, 0), dM1 scalar product formula for cos of the angle, A1 cos = 16/(sqrt72 x sqrt32) = 1/3, A1 awrt 70.5 degrees (1.23 rad); 109.5 followed by 70.5 needs an argument.
path: P4.7.7 - The scalar product. Its use

items.name: Binomial expansion of 27(3-5x)^-2 + Expansion of g(x) using sign change

items.name: Binomial expansion of 27(3-5x)^-2 + Expansion of g(x) using sign change + Expansion of h(x) using scaled x

items.name: Area of parallelogram from vectors + Area of trapezium using parallelogram area

items.name: Separable differential equation with initial condition

items.ms: B1 separate variables with integration, M1 integrate 8y e^(y^2) to 4e^(y^2), A1 4e^(y^2) = x^2/2 (+ c), dM1 use y = 0, x = 5 for c, A1 y^2 = ln((x^2 - 17)/8) with brackets correct.

items.name: Binomial expansion of (4+5x)^(1/2) and combination
items.how: (a) first 4 terms in ascending powers of x of (4 + 5x)^(1/2), simplest form; (b) state the range of x for validity; (c)(i) write down the expansion of (4 - 5x)^(1/2), (ii) show (4 + 5x)^(1/2) + (4 - 5x)^(1/2) = a + bx^2 for small x (the 1/2 power is inferred from the mark scheme).
items.ms: (a) B1 factor 2(1 + 5x/4)^(1/2), M1 binomial structure for the 3rd or 4th term, A1 correct term, A1 two simplified terms, A1 2 + (5/4)x - (25/64)x^2 + (125/512)x^3. (b) B1 |x| < 4/5. (c)(i) B1ft change odd-power signs; (ii) M1 add the two expansions, A1 4 - (25/32)x^2.
path: P4.4.1 - Binomial Series for any rati

items.name: Tangent to implicit curve with exponential term

items.name: Gradient of tangent to parametric curve

items.name: Proof by contradiction on integer quadratic
items.how: You may assume that if n^2 is even then n is even; given p and q integers, use proof by contradiction to show p^2 - 4q + 2 is not 0.
items.ms: B1 assume p^2 - 4q + 2 = 0, M1 p^2 = 4q - 2, A1 p^2 even so p even (p = 2k), dM1 substitute to get e.g. 4k^2 = 4q - 2, A1 a reason (2q - 2k^2 = 1 impossible, or a multiple of 4 against not) and a conclusion that the expression is not 0. An odds-and-evens approach is also accepted.

items.name: Connected rates of change for cube volume + Rate of edge growth at given volume

items.name: Substitution to transform exponential integral + Partial fractions with repeated linear factor + Integrate partial fractions with logarithms

items.name: Connected rates of change, expanding cube
items.how: A cube's volume increases at a constant 0.085 cm^3/s; find the rate of increase of the side length (k cm/s) at the instant V = 100 cm^3, giving the answer to 3 significant figures.
items.ms: B1 for dV/dx = 3x^2; B1 for x = cube root of 100 when V = 100; M1 for dx/dt = (dx/dV) x (dV/dt) with 1/(3x^2) and 0.085, using the numerical x; A1 for awrt 0.00132. Common error: substituting 100 for x instead of for V.

items.name: Cartesian equation from rational parametric form

items.ms: M1 for rearranging x to find t in terms of x and substituting into y; A1 for any correct equation connecting y and x (need not be simplified); A1 for the required form y = (2x + 3)/(18x - 3) with no errors. Marks are lost by algebraic slips when clearing the double fraction.

The assumption statement must be seen.

items.name: Implicit differentiation of quadratic curve

Common losses: missing the product rule on xy and sign errors when rearranging.

items.name: Normal to implicit curve at point

items.name: Prove by contradiction inequality with fractions
items.how: Prove by contradiction that for real a > 0 and b > 0, 9a/b + 4b/a is at least 12 (the inequality is in the form shown in the question).
items.ms: B1 for the set-up: 'assume', positive real a and b, and the negated inequality 9a/b + 4b/a < 12; M1 for multiplying by ab to get 9a^2 + 4b^2 < 12ab; A1 for reaching (3a - 2b)^2 < 0; A1* for the reason (a square cannot be negative) and a conclusion that the original statement holds. Common errors: differentiating 3^x as x 3^(x-1) and A0 for writing dy/dx = ... at the differentiation stage with wrong terms.

(b) M1 for substituting x = 1/20 into both sides and equating; dM1 for a valid method to isolate sqrt(10) as a fraction; A1 for 1359/430 (or 4300/1359 form accepted per scheme for the reciprocal).

items.name: Connected rates of change for expanding rod
items.how: A cylindrical rod of radius x cm and length 6x cm has cross-sectional area increasing at a constant pi/20 cm^2/s; find the rate of increase of volume when x = 2, in the form k pi cm^3/s with k rational.
items.ms: Three B1 marks for dA/dt = pi/20, dA/dx = 2 pi x and dV/dx = 18 pi x^2 (one, two, then all three seen); M1 for a full chain-rule attempt for dV/dt; dM1 for evaluating at x = 2; A1 for 9 pi/10 (k = 0.9). Alternative: V in terms of A (V = 6 pi^(-1/2) A^(3/2)) then dV/dA x dA/dt. Circumference 2 pi x alone does not earn the B1 unless set equal to dA/dx.

items.name: Volume of revolution from parametric equations setup
items.how: For x = 3 sin t, y = 2 sin 2t, 0 <= t <= pi/2, region S is bounded by the curve, the x-axis and a line x = 3/2; show that the volume of revolution is k times the integral of sin^2 t cos^3 t dt from 0 to a, with k and a given in terms of pi.
items.ms: B1 for the upper limit a = pi/6 (from x = 3/2); M1 for pi y^2 dx/dt dt with dx/dt = 3 cos t; dM1 for sin 2t = 2 sin t cos t; A1 cso for 48 pi times the integral of sin^2 t cos^3 t dt from 0 to pi/6. The integral and dt must be shown in the printed form.
path: P4.6.1 - Evaluation of volume of revo

items.name: Evaluate volume integral by substitution u = sin t
items.how: Use the substitution u = sin t, or otherwise, to find the exact value of this volume in the form p pi/q with p, q integers (calculator-only solutions not accepted).
items.ms: B1 for du/dt = cos t; M1 for a full substitution to 48 pi times the integral of u^2(1 - u^2) du; dM1 for multiplying out and integrating to u^3/3 - u^5/5; ddM1 for limits u = 1/2 and 0 (or t = pi/6 and 0) with subtraction; A1 for 17 pi/10 (equivalently 51 pi/30). Condone cos^2 t = 1 - sin^2 t used before substituting.

deps.name: Volume of revolution from parametric equations setup

items.name: Partial fractions then separable differential equation model
items.how: (a) Express 1/((4 - x)(2 - x)) in partial fractions; (b) solve dx/dt = k(4 - x)(2 - x) with x = 0 at t = 0 to show x = (4 - 4e^(2kt))/(1 - 2e^(2kt)) (given); (c) with k = 0.1 find t when x = 1, to 3 significant figures.
items.ms: (a) M1 for A(2 - x) + B(4 - x) = 1 leading to a value; A1 for -1/2 /(4 - x) + 1/2 /(2 - x). (b) M1A1 for separating and integrating to ln(4 - x) and ln(2 - x) terms; M1 for using t = 0, x = 0 to find the constant; M1 for combining logs and exponentiating correctly; dM1 for rearranging to make x the subject; A1* for the given form with all steps shown. (c) M1 for substituting x = 1, k = 0.1 to reach p e^(0.2t) = q; A1 for awrt 2.03.

items.name: Axis intercepts of parametric curve
items.how: For x = t^2 + 2t, y = t^3 - 9t, find the coordinates of A and show B is (15, 0); the curve meets the x-axis at the origin, A and B.
items.ms: M1 for setting y = 0, t^3 - 9t = 0 (or using x = 15 to find t = 3); A1* for substituting t = 3 into x to show x = 15 with working seen and B = (15, 0) stated; B1 for A = (3, 0) (from t = -3). Just stating t = 3 then x = 15 earns M1 but not the A mark.
path: Topic 3 Coordinate geometry in the (x, y) plane

items.name: Tangent to parametric curve at B
items.how: Find the equation of the tangent to the curve at B in the form ax + by + c = 0 with integer a, b, c.
items.ms: M1 for dy/dx = (3t^2 - 9)/(2t + 2) evaluated at t = 3; A1 for 9/4; dM1 for using (15, 0) with their gradient to form the tangent equation; A1 for 9x - 4y - 135 = 0 or an integer multiple.

deps.name: Axis intercepts of parametric curve

items.name: Second intersection of tangent with parametric curve
items.how: The tangent at B meets the curve again at X; use algebra, showing each stage, to find the coordinates of X.
items.ms: M1 for substituting x = t^2 + 2t and y = t^3 - 9t into the tangent to get a cubic in t (4t^3 - 9t^2 - 54t + 135 = 0); dM1 for a non-calculator factorisation using the repeated root t = 3, (t - 3)^2(4t + 15); A1 for t = -15/4; dM1 for finding x or y from their t; A1 for (105/16, -1215/64). Calculator-solved cubics lose the dM1 and A1.

deps.name: Tangent to parametric curve at B

items.name: Find unknown coordinates of points on line
items.how: Line l has vector equation r = (-i - 4j + 6k) + lambda(2i + j - k); A is (1, a, 5) and B is (b, -1, 3); find the constants a and b.
items.ms: M1 for finding lambda at A (using the z-coordinate, lambda = 1) or at B (lambda = 3); A1 for one of a = -3 or b = 5; A1 for both correct.

items.name: Vector between two points on line
items.how: Find the vector AB.
items.ms: M1 for subtracting the position vectors of A and B (either way round; two correct components implies it); A1 for 4i + 2j - 2k with correct vector notation (not coordinates or mixed forms).

deps.name: Find unknown coordinates of points on line

items.name: Angle CAB between vectors at a vertex
items.how: Given C (4, -3, 2), find the size of angle CAB.
items.ms: M1 for AC (or CA) by subtraction; dM1 for the scalar product of AB and AC divided by the product of magnitudes (both magnitudes via a correct method); A1 for 30 degrees (or pi/6). Obtaining cos = -sqrt(3)/2 (150 degrees) from CA with AB scores A0 unless corrected to angle CAB.

deps.name: Vector between two points on line
Find unknown coordinates of points on line

items.name: Exact area of triangle from vectors
items.how: Find the exact area of triangle CAB.

A modulus method gives 6 lambda^2 ... = 96 leading to lambda = 5, -3 and must substitute back into the line.

Vector between two points on line

items.name: Volume of revolution under reciprocal curve
items.how: Region R is bounded by the curve y = 4/(x + 2) (x > -2), the y-axis, the x-axis and x = 8, and is rotated through 360 degrees about the x-axis; use calculus to find the exact volume in simplest form, showing all stages.
items.ms: B1 for pi times the integral of (4/(x + 2))^2 dx from 0 to 8 (limits and 16 pi seen or implied); M1 for integrating to a -16/(x + 2) form; A1 for the correct integral; M1 for substituting 0 and 8 and subtracting; A1 for 32 pi/5. Common errors: omitting the squaring or pi, and ln integration of (x + 2)^-2.
path: P4.6.1 - Evaluation of volume of revo

items.name: Implicit differentiation with exponential term
items.how: For the curve 3x + 5y^2 + 4x^2 y = 10(2^x) + 35, y > 0, find an expression for dy/dx in terms of x and y.
items.ms: B1 for d/dx of 2^x = 2^x ln 2; M1 for 5y^2 giving a multiple of y dy/dx; M1 for the product rule on 4x^2 y; A1 for fully correct differentiation; M1 for factorising dy/dx from exactly the two correct terms and dividing; A1 for dy/dx = (10(2^x) ln 2 - 3 - 8xy)/(10y + 4x^2).

items.name: Exact gradient at y-axis intercept
items.how: C cuts the y-axis at P; find the exact value of the gradient of the tangent to C at P.
items.ms: M1 for putting x = 0 into the equation of C to find y = 3 and substituting into dy/dx; A1 for (10 ln 2 - 3)/30 or equivalent, from the correct gradient expression, with only one answer (y = -3 rejected).

deps.name: Implicit differentiation with exponential term

items.name: Binomial expansion of reciprocal square root, find constants
items.how: Given that the binomial expansion in ascending powers of x of 6/sqrt(4 + Ax) is B - x/4 + C x^2 + ..., find the constants A, B and C.
items.ms: B1 for B = 3 (taking out the factor 4^(-1/2) times 6); M1 for equating the x coefficient, (-1/2)(A/4) times 3 = -1/4; A1 for A = 2/3; M1 for the x^2 term using (-1/2)(-3/2)/2! with their A; A1 for C = 1/32.
path: P4.4.1 - Binomial Series for any rati

items.name: Validity range of binomial expansion
items.how: State the range of values of x for which this expansion is valid.
items.ms: B1ft for |x| < 6 (i.e. |Ax/4| < 1 with their A); strict or non-strict end points condoned; accepted in interval notation.

deps.name: Binomial expansion of reciprocal square root, find constants

path: P4.4.1 - Binomial Series for any rati

items.name: Coefficient of x cubed in binomial expansion
items.how: For the expansion, find the coefficient of the term in x^3.
items.ms: M1 for 3 x (-1/2)(-3/2)(-5/2)/3! x (A/4)^3 with their A; A1 for -5/1152. Correct answer with correct work in part (a) earns both marks.

deps.name: Binomial expansion of reciprocal square root, find constants

items.name: Balloon rate of change and separable water depth model
items.how: (i) A spherical balloon's volume increases at a constant 70 pi cm^3/s; find the rate of increase of the radius when r = 5 (V = (4/3) pi r^3 given); (ii) solve dh/dt = k/h^3 with h = 4 at t = 0 and h = 6 at t = 5 to find T when h = 10, to one decimal place; show all stages.
items.ms: (i) B1 dV/dt = 70 pi; B1 dV/dr = 4 pi r^2; M1 chain rule with r = 5; A1 for 0.7 cm/s. (ii) M1A1 for separating and integrating to (1/4)h^4 = kt + c; M1 for using t = 0, h = 4 (c = 64); dM1 for t = 5, h = 6 to find k = 52; dddM1 for h = 10 to find T; A1 for T = 46.8 (609/13). A constant of integration is needed.

items.name: Integration by parts twice and partial fractions definite integral
items.how: (i) Find the integral of x^2 e^(4x) dx in simplest form; (ii) use partial fractions and algebraic integration to show the integral of (2x + 11)/((2x + 1)(2 - x)) dx from 4 to 7 equals ln k with k a fully simplified rational constant to be found.
items.ms: (i) M1A1 for parts the right way round (minus sign present); dM1 for parts again on x e^(4x); A1 for (1/4)x^2 e^(4x) - (1/8)x e^(4x) + (1/32)e^(4x) + c. (ii) M1 for partial fractions of the correct form; A1 for 4/(2x + 1) + 3/(2 - x); dM1A1ft for 2ln|2x + 1| - 3ln|2 - x| with brackets or moduli; ddM1 for limits 4 and 7 subtracted; A1 for ln(8/45). Common errors: ln(2 - x) without modulus and missing factors of 2 when integrating.

items.name: Proof by contradiction, even quadratic implies odd n
items.how: Given n is a natural number, use algebra to prove by contradiction that if n^2 - 4n + 5 is even then n is odd.
items.ms: B1 for the assumption in words, n^2 - 4n + 5 is even and n is even; M1 for n = 2k substituted; A1 for 4k^2 - 8k + 5; A1* for a clearly odd form (e.g. 4(k^2 - 2k) + 5), the statement 'which is odd', and a conclusion such as contradiction, hence proven. Assuming the negation with odd/odd scores no marks. B0M1A1A1 is not possible.

items.name: Trigonometric substitution for definite integral with power denominator
items.how: Showing all stages, use the substitution x = 4 sin(theta) to find the exact value of the integral of 1/(16 - x^2)^(3/2) dx between the given limits (2 and 2 sqrt(3)).
items.ms: B1 for dx/dtheta = 4 cos theta; M1 for simplifying (16 - x^2)^(3/2) to k cos^3 theta using the Pythagorean identity; A1 for the integrand (1/16) sec^2 theta (or equivalent); dM1 for integrating to (1/16) tan theta; M1 for limits pi/6 and pi/3 (30 and 60 degrees) subtracted; A1 for sqrt(3)/24 (or 1/(8 sqrt(3))).

items.name: Angle CAB in degrees from scalar product
items.how: Given C (4, 7, -2), find the size of angle CAB in degrees to one decimal place.
items.ms: M1 for AC by subtracting OA from OC; dM1 for the scalar product of AC and AB (72 + 60 + 18); ddM1 for dividing by the magnitudes, cos(theta) = 150/(sqrt(172) sqrt(189)); A1 for awrt 33.7 degrees. The cosine rule with all three sides is an accepted alternative.

Modulus method gives 21 lambda^2 + 42 lambda - 735 = 0 and must be substituted back into the line.

items.name: Parametric gradient and tangent equation at P
items.how: For x = 2cos 2t, y = sin^3 t with P at t = pi/6, use parametric differentiation to show (i) dy/dx = k sin t with k to be found and (ii) the tangent l has equation 3x + 16y - 5 = 0 (given).
items.ms: (i) M1 for dy/dx = (dy/dt)/(dx/dt); A1 for (3 sin^2 t cos t)/(-4 sin 2t); A1 for -(3/8) sin t using sin 2t = 2 sin t cos t. (ii) B1 for P = (1, 1/8); M1 for gradient -3/16 and y - y1 = m(x - x1); A1* for 3x + 16y - 5 = 0, cso (withheld if (i) was fortuitous).

items.name: Second intersection of tangent with parametric curve
items.how: The tangent l meets C again at Q; using algebra and showing detailed reasoning, find the exact coordinates of Q.
items.ms: M1 for substituting x = 2cos 2t and y = sin^3 t into 3x + 16y - 5 = 0; dM1 for cos 2t = 1 - 2 sin^2 t to get a cubic in sin t; A1 for 16 sin^3 t - 12 sin^2 t + 1 = 0; ddM1 for solving (calculator allowed) for sin t other than 1/2; dddM1 for sin t = -1/4 substituted into x and y; A1 for Q = (7/4, -1/64). Eliminating t to a cubic in x or y is an alternative.

items.name: Unknown constants for points on a line + Vector AB from points on line

items.name: Validity range of binomial expansion

items.name: Definite integral of x cubed times logarithm
items.how: Using algebraic integration, find the exact value of the integral of x^3 ln(x/2) dx between limits 2 and 2e^2 (form per the mark scheme), giving the answer in simplest form, showing all stages.
items.ms: M1 for parts the correct way round (ln differentiated, x^3 integrated); dM1 for integrating again to px^4 ln(x/2) - qx^4; A1 for (1/4)x^4 ln(x/2) - (1/16)x^4; ddM1 for substituting both limits and subtracting with ln(e^2) = 2 and ln 1 = 0; A1 for 7e^8 + 1 in simplest form. A substitution u = x/2 is an accepted alternative.

items.name: Factorise then prove no integer solutions by contradiction
items.how: (a) Factorise x^2 - 4y^2; (b) use proof by contradiction to prove there are no positive integers x and y with x^2 - 4y^2 = 27.
items.ms: (a) B1 for (x + 2y)(x - 2y). (b) M1 for one valid pair of equations, x + 2y = 27 with x - 2y = 1, or x + 2y = 9 with x - 2y = 3; A1 for correctly solving one pair (y = 6.5 or y = 1.5); dM1 for stating and solving both valid pairs; A1* for the full proof: set-up with 'assume there are positive integers', both pairs solved (non-integer y), and a conclusion. Alternative: x odd, x = 2m + 1, giving y^2 non-integer.

items.name: Substitution then partial fractions definite integral
items.how: (a) Use the substitution u = e^x + 4 to show the integral of (2e^x + 3)/(e^x + 4) dx from 0 to ln 6 equals the integral of (cu + d)/(u(u - 4)) du between limits a and b to be found; (b) hence, using algebraic integration, show the integral equals P ln 2 + Q ln 3 with P and Q to be found.
items.ms: (a) B1 for limits 5 and 10; M1 for du/dx = e^x = u - 4 and rewriting in u; A1 for (2u - 5)/(u(u - 4)) du with integral sign and du shown. (b) B1 for setting up partial fractions A/u + B/(u - 4); M1 for a valid method for A and B; A1 for A = 5/4, B = 3/4; M1 for integrating to ln u and ln(u - 4) terms; dM1 for limits 5 and 10 with log laws; A1 for 2 ln 2 + (3/4) ln 3.

items.name: Domain and range of Cartesian function of curve
items.how: Given the Cartesian equation of C is y = f(x), defined for all x on C, find (i) the domain of f and (ii) the range of f.
items.ms: (i) M1 for the correct upper or lower bound of x (x = -5 at t = 0, x tends to 2 as t tends to infinity); A1 for -5 <= x < 2 in correct notation. (ii) B1 for f(x) >= 2 (minimum y at t = 1), not written with x.

items.name: Point on line nearest the origin

items.ms: M1 for setting OP perpendicular to l1 (scalar product with the direction = 0) or minimising |OP|^2, and solving for lambda; A1 for lambda = 3/2 (setting the x-coordinate to 0 scores nothing); dM1 for substituting lambda into the line; A1 for P = (0, 3/2, 1/2) with correct notation.

items.ms: M1 for equating the x and z components and solving for lambda and mu (-3 + 2 lambda = 4 mu, 5 - 3 lambda = -2 mu); A1 for lambda = 7/4, mu = 1/8; dM1 for using the y components, lambda = mu a; A1 for a = 14.

items.name: Coordinates of lines' point of intersection
items.how: Find the coordinates of Q.
items.ms: M1 for substituting lambda (or mu and a) into either line equation; A1 for Q = (1/2, 7/4, -1/4) with correct notation.

items.name: x coordinates at given y on implicit curve
items.how: Curve C has equation 32y^2/pi^2 + x^2 tan y = 11; points P and Q have the same given y coordinate (pi/4); find their x coordinates.
items.ms: M1 for substituting y = pi/4 with tan(pi/4) = 1 and getting x^2 = 9; A1 for x = 3 and x = -3 (P at 3, Q at -3).

items.name: Time for balloon to fully deflate
items.how: Given that V = 0 when t = T, use the model to find T to one decimal place.
items.ms: M1 for setting r = 0 in their r = n(A - Bt)^(1/3) form and solving for T; A1 for awrt 25.6. Alternative via the constant rate of volume loss.

items.name: Find a and n from binomial expansion coefficients + Cubic coefficient p of binomial expansion
items.how: Hence find the value of p, the coefficient of x^3.
