items.name: Coordinates of point on parametric curve + Parametric derivative of rational curve + Tangent to parametric curve at point P
items.how: Hence find the equation of the tangent to C at P in the form y = mx + c.
items.ms: M1 for evaluating their dy/dx at t = 3 (28) and using it with their point P in y - y1 = m(x - x1); A1cso for y = 28x - 18.

items.name: Exact gradient by implicit differentiation at P + Product of tangent and normal gradients
items.how: Hence, showing working, find (gradient of tangent at P) x (gradient of normal at Q).
items.ms: M1 for finding the gradient of the tangent at Q by substituting x = -3, y = pi/4 (or by symmetry, opposite of P's gradient); A1 for product = 1, from exact gradients at P and Q (the normal gradient is the negative reciprocal).

items.name: Derive radius rate equation for deflating balloon + Solve radius differential equation with two conditions
items.how: Given initial radius 30 cm and radius 12 cm after 24 s, solve the differential equation in part (a) to find an equation for r in terms of t.
items.ms: M1 for separating variables and integrating to ...r^3 = ...t (+ c); A1 for (1/3)r^3 = -kt + c; M1 for t = 0, r = 30 giving a non-zero constant (c = 9000); ddM1 for t = 24, r = 12 to find k (351); A1 for r = cube root of (27000 - 1053t). Using an incorrect k value limits the marks to the first two.

items.name: Set up volume of revolution from parametric curve + Evaluate volume integral for exact value
items.how: Hence, using algebraic integration, find the exact value of V.
items.ms: M1 for writing sin^2 t cos^3 t as sin^2 t (1 - sin^2 t) cos t (or u = sin t substitution); dM1 for integrating to (1/3)sin^3 t - (1/5)sin^5 t (or u^3/3 - u^5/5); ddM1 for limits 0 and pi/2 (0 and 1); A1 for V = 80 pi. Equally acceptable via x = 6 sin t.

items.name: Possible y values at given x on implicit curve
items.how: Curve C is 2y^2 - 6xy = 7e^(2x - 1) + 13 (as read from the mark scheme); P has x coordinate 1/2; find the two possible y coordinates of P, showing all stages.
items.ms: M1 for substituting x = 1/2, collecting a 3-term quadratic in y (2y^2 - 3y - 20 = 0) and solving; A1 for y = -5/2 and y = 4. A calculator may solve the quadratic if the quadratic is correct.

items.name: Tangent to implicit curve with exponential term
items.how: Given P lies above the x-axis, find an equation of the tangent to C at P in the form ax + by + c = 0 with integers a, b, c.
items.ms: B1 for 2y^2 differentiating to 4y dy/dx; M1 for the product rule on -6xy; A1 for 4y dy/dx - 6x dy/dx - 6y = 14e^(2x-1); M1 for substituting x = 1/2 and y = 4 (exactly two dy/dx terms) to get 38/13; M1 for the tangent equation through (1/2, 4); A1 for 38x - 13y + 33 = 0 (or integer multiple).

deps.name: Possible y values at given x on implicit curve

items.name: Melting ice ball rate inversely proportional to r squared
items.how: A ball of ice of radius r has volume V = (4/3) pi r^3 decreasing at a constant rate k cm^3/s; show that the rate of decrease of the radius is inversely proportional to the square of the radius.
items.ms: B1 for dV/dt = k (or -k); B1 for dV/dr = 4 pi r^2; M1 for the chain rule dV/dt = dV/dr x dr/dt; A1* for dr/dt = k/(4 pi r^2) with a valid reason (k and pi constants) and a conclusion. All previous marks are needed for the A1*.

items.name: Separable differential equation with trigonometric terms
items.how: Given y = 4 at x = pi/6, solve y cos^2(2x) dy/dx = 3 sin 2x, giving the answer in the form y^2 = g(x).
items.ms: M1 for separating variables (y dy = 3 sin 2x/cos^2 2x dx); A1 for correct separation with sec 2x tan 2x or an equivalent form; M1 for integrating the x side to a sec 2x (or 1/cos 2x) form; A1 for y^2/2 = (3/2) sec 2x; dM1 for using x = pi/6, y = 4 to find the constant (5); A1 for y^2 = 3 sec 2x + 10 (equivalently 3/cos 2x + 10).

items.name: Normal to parametric curve at given point
items.how: For x = (3 + 2t)/(1 - t), y = 1 - t^2, use parametric differentiation to find the equation of the normal at P (t = 2) in the form ax + by + c = 0 with integers.
items.ms: M1 for dy/dx = (dy/dt)/(dx/dt), with dx/dt = 5/(1 - t)^2 via the quotient rule and dy/dt = -2t, evaluated at t = 2; A1 for -4/5 (or normal gradient 5/4); B1 for P = (-7, -3); M1 for the normal using the negative reciprocal; A1 for 5x - 4y + 23 = 0. A Cartesian route scores at most the B1.

items.name: Cartesian equation of rational parametric curve
items.how: Show that a Cartesian equation for C can be written y = (px + q)/(x + r)^2, x not equal to k, with integers p, q, r and k to be found.
items.ms: M1 for making t the subject of the x equation, t = (x - 3)/(x + 2); dM1 for substituting into y = 1 - t^2 and combining into a single fraction; A1 for y = (10x - 5)/(x + 2)^2; B1 for the exclusion x not equal to -2 (k = -2).
path: Topic 3 Coordinate geometry in the (x, y) plane

items.name: Vector equation of line through A and B
items.how: Given position vectors of A and B, write down a vector equation for the line l through A and B.
items.ms: M1 for the difference of the position vectors (direction 4i + 4k, two correct components implying it); A1 for any correct equation of the form r = ..., e.g. r = i + 2j - 3k + lambda(4i + 4k). Writing 'l =' is A0.

items.name: Unknown component from angle at vertex
items.how: Given C = 3i + alpha j + 5k and angle BAC = 45 degrees, find the exact possible values of alpha.

items.name: Binomial series approximation for root of 135
items.how: (a) Find the first three non-zero terms of the binomial expansion of 1/sqrt(4 + x), coefficients as simplified fractions; (b) using (a), state the first three terms of 1/sqrt(4 - x); (c) hence or otherwise show 1/sqrt(16 - x^2) is approximately a + bx^2 with a, b fully simplified fractions; (d) use this with x = 1 to find a fully simplified rational approximation for sqrt(135).
items.ms: (a) M1 for factor 4^(-1/2) out; M1 for a correct third term (-1/2)(-3/2)/2! with its power of x; A1 for two correct simplified terms; A1 for 1/2 - x/16 + 3x^2/256. items.name: Disprove trig inequality by contradiction on interval
items.how: Showing all stages, use proof by contradiction to show that for all angles x with 90 degrees < x < 180 degrees, |cos 2x/(cos x - sin x)| < 1.
items.ms: B1 for the assumption (an angle x in the interval with the modulus quotient at least 1); M1 for cos 2x = (cos x + sin x)(cos x - sin x) and simplifying to |cos x + sin x| >= 1; dM1 for squaring and using sin^2 + cos^2 = 1 to reach sin 2x >= 0; A1* for the contradiction (sin 2x < 0 since 180 < 2x < 360) with a conclusion, and the modulus handled correctly. R-alpha form 2cos(x - 45) is an alternative.

items.name: Partial fractions with three linear factors + Exact definite integral of partial fractions with logs
